# Fitness status — 2026-09-22

Window: 2026-08-26 to 2026-09-22 (28 days)

## Summary

_Note: this report uses a 28-day window instead of the default 14 so it can answer a "last four weeks" question. The snapshot comes from `build_fitness_status(days=28)`. The config default was not changed._

**Training load & consistency.** 20 activities in 28 days: 14 runs (98.5 km, about 14.2 h; includes a "Lugano Hiking" logged as street running on 26 Aug and the Monte Brè trail run on 20 Sep), 3 road rides (124.5 km, 7.3 h), 1 hike (Alagna, 8.6 km, 5 h) and 2 short walks. Week by week: running was 5 runs / 31.0 km (26 Aug–1 Sep), then 3 runs each week at 22.3, 23.2 and 22.0 km, plus one ride a week of 44, 30 and 50 km. The pattern is very steady (3 runs + 1 ride), but running volume has not grown since the first week. Garmin's chronic (28-day) load went from 287 to 337 (+17%). Acute load dropped to 126–166 during the easy stretch on 9–10 Sep and is now back at 409 (ACWR 1.2). Training status went from PRODUCTIVE (late Aug), to MAINTAINING, to NO_STATUS (1–10 Sep, data gap), to UNPRODUCTIVE (11–12 Sep), to MAINTAINING, and is now PRODUCTIVE again (20–22 Sep). Flat-run efficiency is slightly better: on 16 Sep you ran 8.0 km at 7:05/km with an average HR of 135, compared with 5.0 km at 6:57/km and HR 138 on 31 Aug. You went further at almost the same pace with slightly lower HR. This is a modest gain, not a big jump. Intensity is almost all aerobic base: Garmin reports "AEROBIC_HIGH_SHORTAGE" in both late August and today (high-aerobic load 254 against a target of 409–737; anaerobic 31 against 109–327).

**Recovery signals.** Comparing 26–31 Aug with 16–22 Sep: sleep score rose from 67 to 77 on average and average stress fell from 34 to 29. Morning training readiness rose from 46 (all LOW/MODERATE) to 67, and Body Battery peaks rose from 64 to 76. HRV last-night average rose from 44.7 to 47.3 ms, and the weekly HRV went from 45–46 to 47–50, BALANCED throughout. Resting HR did **not** improve: 50.2 then vs 50.9 bpm now (7-day average 51 in both periods). Sleep duration fell from 8.0 h to 7.6 h per night, with short nights of 6.1 h (18 Sep) and 6.5 h (19 Sep) just before the weekend. The best week was 9–15 Sep, right after a lighter spell: readiness averaged 82 (100/PRIME on 10 Sep), HRV averaged 51 and sleep score 81. As load came back, those numbers slipped. The weekend block (50 km ride on 19 Sep, Monte Brè on 20 Sep, run on 21 Sep) pushed readiness down to 28 (LOW) on 21 Sep, with sleep score 53 and a Body Battery low of 5. It recovered to 58 (MODERATE) today after a good night (8.8 h, score 87). **Missing data:** from 1 to 7 Sep there are no sleep, HRV, resting-HR or stress records (the watch was probably not worn). 8 Sep has resting HR (54) and stress but no sleep or HRV. Readiness and training status values exist for those days but were computed without sleep input, so treat them with caution.

**VO2max trend.** Per-run watch values (runs only): 31 Aug 41, 1 Sep 40, 2 Sep 40, 4 Sep 39, 6 Sep 39, 11 Sep 39, 13 Sep 40, 14 Sep 40, 16 Sep 40, 21 Sep 40. The runs from 26–28 Aug and the trail run on 20 Sep have no value. Overall it is flat at 39–41, which is normal noise. The account-level trend in `training_status` was null until 11 Sep. Since then it has risen from 39.6 (11 Sep) to 40.3, 40.2, 40.4 and 40.7 (21 Sep, shown as 41). That is a small but steady rise of about 1 point in 10 days. It is encouraging, but too small to call a real fitness change yet.

**Observations / suggestions.**
1. The easy volume is consistent, but it has been stuck at about 22 km/week of running for three weeks, and Garmin keeps reporting a shortage of high-aerobic work. Replacing one of the three weekly runs with a tempo or interval session is the most likely way to move VO2max beyond the current ±1 noise.
2. Recovery is better than four weeks ago (readiness +20, sleep score +10, HRV +2.6 ms), but resting HR is flat at about 50–51 and nightly sleep is 0.4 h shorter. Big weekend blocks after short nights (6.1 h and 6.5 h on 18–19 Sep) are what drove readiness down to 28. Protecting sleep before long rides or hilly runs would help.
3. Today readiness is 58 (MODERATE) with about 5.6 h of recovery time left and ACWR 1.2. Keep today easy or rest, and put the next quality session on a day when readiness is back above 70.
